questions.q: Tell me about your recruiting work. What roles did you hire for, which sources did you use, and how many positions did you close in a month?
questions.looks_for: Real roles and levels, sources (job portals, referrals, LinkedIn, walk-ins), monthly numbers, and their own part from sourcing to joining.

questions.q: Describe a hard position you filled. Why was it hard and what did you do differently to close it?
questions.looks_for: Specific role and challenge (rare skill, low budget, location), new sourcing or screening steps, talks with the hiring manager, and the final result.

questions.q: How do you screen a resume and a first phone call to decide if a candidate should go to the hiring manager?
questions.looks_for: Matches must-have skills and experience, checks gaps and job changes sensibly, confirms salary, notice and location on the call, and judges communication fairly.

questions.q: Why do candidates drop out after accepting an offer, and what can a recruiter do to reduce it?
questions.looks_for: Counter offers, better offers, long notice, poor communication; stays in touch, clear offer details, early salary talk, regular follow-up till joining.

questions.q: What questions should a recruiter never ask a candidate, and why?
questions.looks_for: Nothing on religion, caste, marriage, pregnancy, family plans, age or similar; unfair, can be illegal, and hiring should be on skills only.

questions.q: A hiring manager rejects five good candidates in a row without clear reasons, and the role is urgent. What would you do?
questions.looks_for: Asks for specific feedback, revisits the job requirements together, aligns on must-haves, shares market data on salary or skills, and adjusts the search politely.

questions.q: Why do you want this HR recruiter job, when can you join (state your notice period), and what salary do you expect?
questions.looks_for: Clear reason linked to the work, states notice period or joining date in days or weeks, and gives an expected monthly or yearly salary figure or range without dodging.
